findings.title: Stolen session cookies retain access after password changes
findings.why_it_matters: Updating only password_hash preserves the session signing secret. An attacker can replay a previously stolen triggarr_session cookie after the owner changes their password: AuthMiddleware (triggarr/web/middleware.py:144–148) accepts it using validate_session, which checks only the signature and 30-day expiry, never the password hash. Removing secret rotation therefore preserves attacker access for the cookie’s remaining lifetime. Existing session-eviction tests explicitly require the opposite behavior.
